threads.body: An explicitly configured name is not always distinguishable by comparing values. For example, if this instance's generated name is `p1` and the application calls `setName("p1")` (or supplies that value through `Properties`), this returns `false` and the start advice replaces the explicitly configured name with the derived database name, contrary to the PR's preservation guarantee. Track whether `setName` was invoked (for example, with a boolean `VirtualField` and setter advice, as the Tomcat JDBC instrumentation does) rather than inferring intent from equality.

[Naming] `VirtualField` is a semantic handle under the Java style guide, so this field should use `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. Please rename `configuredNameField` to `CONFIGURED_NAME_FIELD` and update both references below.

[General] This adds a public library API, but the library README still documents only the single-argument `registerMetrics`. Please add a short explicit-pool-name usage example, as the equivalent c3p0 change did, so library users can discover this option.

`metadata.yaml` still describes the module generically, so the published instrumentation list will not mention the derived `server.address[:server.port][/db.namespace]` pool name or the `vibur-dbcp` fallback. Tomcat JDBC and Apache DBCP document this in their metadata descriptions.
